conflicts.topic: temperature dependence of Hall-Petch slope and friction stress in HEAs
conflicts.claim_a: Previous work reported that the Hall-Petch slope and friction stress of CoCrFeMnNi HEAs both increase with decreasing temperature.
conflicts.claim_b: Wu et al. concluded that the temperature-dependent yield strength results from the temperature dependence of friction stress, not Hall-Petch slopes, which did not vary with temperature in FeNiCoCr HEAs.

evidence.quote: It is also interesting that with th e decrease of temperature, a significant increase occurred in the value of Hall-Petch slope and the friction stress in CoCrFeMnNi HEAs [15]. In contrast, Wu et al. conclu ded that the temperature-dependent yield strength is resulted fr om the temperature dependence of friction stress, not Hall-Petch slopes, which did n ot vary with temperature in FeNiCoCr HEAs [29].
